title: Introduce zero-copy message frames and unified I/O executor to reduce CPU overhead
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Reduced CPU overhead on request path by introducing zero-copy message frames and consolidating I/O executors. Expected improvements: ~18-30% CPU reduction on snapshot workloads and lower tail latency under high concurrency.
description: Context: Production traces and perf lab runs identified significant CPU overhead from repeated buffer copies and cross-executor handoffs on the hot request path, especially for small prompt/response workloads and KV cache hits. Motivation: Reduce per-request CPU work by eliminating redundant copies, consolidating executor queues to reduce syscall/context-switch churn, and provide a safe zero-copy abstraction that integrates with existing KV cache and batching layers. Summary of changes: 1) protocol: add MessageFrame abstraction as refcounted, slice-backed frame that can represent socket buffers, mmaped segments, or rental-backed vectors; 2) zero-copy path: implement splice-like fast-paths to forward socket buffers into the runtime without copying when frames are owned by the network stack; 3) unified I/O executor: replace separate net and disk executors with a unified_io_executor that holds a small set of worker threads pinned with soft affinity hints and uses a per-thread submission queue to avoid global locks; 4) scheduler integration: scheduler now recognizes MessageFrame lifetimes and will avoid materializing copies during KV cache lookup/hit and during continuous batching; 5) KV cache: introduce cache::peek_frame API to return borrowed frames to avoid deserialize/re-serialize on hits; 6) safety and fallbacks: non-supporting platforms fall back to existing copy path; extensive asserts and sanitizer builds ensure frame lifetimes are adhered to; 7) benchmarks + perf tests: add microbenchmarks and an end-to-end canary showing CPU and latency improvements. Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4 add MessageFrame type, refcounting and pooling - 2b3c4d5 zero-copy socket->frame splice implementation - 3c4d5e6 unify net/disk executors into unified_io_executor - 4d5e6f7 integrate frame-backed KV cache peek API - 5e6f7g8 scheduler: batch-aware frame forwarding + tests - 6f7g8h9 add benches and perf dashboard links Files changed (high-level): src/proto/message_frame.rs, src/runtime/unified_io_executor.rs, src/runtime/scheduler.rs, src/kv/cache.rs, src/runtime/affinity.rs, benches/zero_copy_kv.rs, tests/ci/zero_copy_smoke.rs, docs/perf/zero_copy.md, scripts/bench/run_zero_copy.sh Review conversation summary: Raj: "Nice targeted change; can we guarantee frame lifetimes across async awaits?" Author(Maya): "Added strong ownership annotations and asserts; see message_frame.rs lines 200-260; scheduler only forwards borrowed references when callback context ensures lifetime." Elena: "Unified executor looks like it could starve lower-priority disk IO under extreme load." Author: "Added cooperative yielding and a per-worker rate limiter; updated scheduler to demote long-running IO tasks." Oliver: "CI flaky on macOS due to missing splice fallback; please add test." Author: "Added fallback path and OS detection; re-ran CI." CI: Initial run failed on macOS and one flaky benchmark; fix committed and final CI status is pass. Performance numbers: Microbench: 18-28% CPU reduction on small prompt steady-state; E2E canary: p95 latency improved by 10-15% under 2k RPS with 8 workers, and tail CPU consumption reduced by ~22%. Backwards compatibility: Non-supporting kernels/platforms fall back to copy path; API surface is internal-only and guarded by feature flags. Risks and mitigations: Memory pinning and refcounts increase complexity and potential leaks; mitigation: added extensive unit tests, sanitizer builds, and a runtime assertion that drops frames detected during shutdown. Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated capacity pools for 48 hours, monitor cpu/tokens-per-second, KV cache hit ratio and errors; enable global rollout after 2 canaries without regressions. Follow-ups: - extend zero-copy to batching layer merges - expose per-tenant executor knobs in Console - add metrics for frame allocations and zero-copy hit rate Merge: Squash merged to main on 2024-11-12. Related items: Linear ENG-4821 (cpu hotpath reductions), ENG-4988 (kv cache optimization). Notes: This PR intentionally centralizes network and disk I/O handling into a single executor to reduce handoff costs; please review affinity heuristics in src/runtime/affinity.rs and the fail-open fallback in message_frame.rs for platform coverage.
